function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a quick snapshot of **major U.S. festivals** that are slated to take place in the coming months (based largely on their usual annual calendars).  
*(Dates are tentative—always double‑check each event’s official site as they’re subject to change.)*

| # | Festival | Typical Date Range* | City / State | What It Is • Highlights | Official Site |
|---|----------|---------------------|--------------|------------------------|---------------|
| 1 | **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | Mid‑April (e.g., Apr 12‑14, 2025) | Indio, California | Two‑weekend outdoor music & art extravaganza featuring headliners from pop, rock, hip‑hop, indie, electronic, plus visual installations. | <https://www.coachellafestival.com> |
| 2 | **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | Early‑mid June (Jun 11‑15, 2025) | Manchester, Tennessee | Three‑day multi‑genre jam‑session with live performances, comedy, dance, yoga, and interactive art spaces. | <https://bonnaroo.com> |
| 3 | **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | Late‑April into early May (Apr 26‑May 04, 2025) | New Orleans, Louisiana | Celebration of jazz, blues, zydeco, world music, along with Cajun cuisine, crafts, and parades. | <https://jazzfest.org> |
| 4 | **South By Southwest (SXSW)** | March‑early April (Mar 17‑28, 2025) | Austin, Texas | Global convergence of film, media, tech, and music industries; includes concerts, panels, networking, and screenings. | <https://sxsw.com> |
| 5 | **Lollapalooza Chicago** | August (Aug 02‑03, 2025) | Chicago, Illinois | One‑night mega‑concert showcasing mainstream and emerging acts across multiple stages. | <https://lolla.com/chicago> |
| 6 | **Burning Man** | Aug 27‑Sep 04, 2025 | Black Rock Desert, Nevada | Radical self‑expression art installation and community gathering in the desert; participants build temporary city structures. | <https://burningman.org> |
| 7 | **Taste of Chicago** | July (Jul 01‑08, 2025) | Chicago, Illinois | Foodie fest offering tastings from over 200 restaurants, cooking demos, and entertainment. | <https://tasteofchicago.com> |

\*These dates reflect the *typical* calendar year‑to‑year. Some festivals shift slightly depending on weekends, holidays, or special circumstances.

---

### How to Find Your Next Local Fest

If you’d rather discover something closer to home, try one of these approaches:

| Tool | Why Use It | Quick Tips |
|------|------------|-----------|
| Google “[city] festivals” | Gives current listings for your area | Add “this week”, “summer”, or specific genres (“food”, “music”) |
| Eventbrite / Meetup | Shows niche gatherings (art shows, book clubs, foodie meetups) | Filter by distance, category, and date range |
| Facebook Events | Community‑curated events often free or low cost | Search “events near me” → filter by “Music”, “Food”, “Arts” |
| Local tourism boards | Often maintain a “What’s On” page | Check state or county websites for seasonal fairs, farmers markets, street festivals |

Feel free to let me know if you want details on a particular genre (like folk, EDM, culinary, family‑friendly, etc.), a specific region, or even how to plan travel around a big festival!
